title: 11 Back Exercises, Ranked for Your Next Pull Day
caption:
Our upper-back picks, ranked from #11 to #1. We favor stable setups and straightforward progression. Which one would you put at #1?

LIFTCODE builds your routine around your goals and gym equipment. Link in bio.

slides.name: 11 Upper-Back Exercises, Ranked
text:
11 BACK EXERCISES
RANKED FOR YOUR
NEXT PULL DAY
Find the right rows for your routine.

slides.name: #11 Face Pulls
text:
Useful for rear delts and upper-back accessory work.
Use a weight you can pull without leaning back.

slides.name: #10 Suspension Row
text:
Change your body angle to make these harder.
Adding weight takes more planning than on a machine.

slides.name: #9 Dumbbell Bent-Over Row
text:
Your lower back has to hold your torso in position.
Row the dumbbells without swinging your body.

slides.name: #8 Seal Row
text:
Chest support limits how much you can swing.
The setup needs enough room below the bench.

slides.name: #7 Barbell Bent-Over Row
text:
A classic way to row heavy, with no chest support.
Your lower back may tire before your upper back.

slides.name: #6 Wide-Grip Cable Row
text:
The wide grip lets you pull with your elbows out.
Keep your torso steady as you add weight.

slides.name: #5 Chest-Supported Dumbbell Row
text:
Chest support helps limit swinging.
Getting heavy dumbbells into position can be awkward.

slides.name: #4 Smith Machine Row
text:
The rails guide the bar, but your chest is unsupported.
Your lower back still has to hold you in position.

slides.name: Just train your back. We’ll build your plan.
text:
JUST TRAIN YOUR BACK.
WE’LL BUILD YOUR PLAN.

to build a routine that fits you.

slides.name: #3 Chest-Supported Machine Row
text:
The chest pad helps you keep your torso still.
Changing the weight is quick.

slides.name: #2 Chest-Supported T-Bar Row
text:
Chest support lets you focus on the pull.
Keep your chest on the pad as you add weight.

slides.name: #1 Kelso Shrugs
text:
Our top pick for shoulder-blade retraction.
Keep your elbows straight as you squeeze your shoulder blades together.

Track your next pull day.

sources.supports: Unsupported bent-over rowing demands trunk work; this study does not validate exercise rank or prove fatigue order for everyone.
Chest pad supports positioning; removing contact increases stabilization demand; controlled torso and return.
Middle trapezius and rhomboids retract scapulae; not a Kelso-versus-all-rows hypertrophy comparison.
Rear deltoids participate in rowing; existing upper-back-only artwork is selective highlighting, not a complete activation map.

rankingStatus: User reference order retained. Practical editorial ranking; no study establishes this exact hierarchy.
imageStatus: User-selected upper-back-only highlighting preserved; does not imply no deltoid recruitment.
